reading.body:
This record is a mistag rather than a data center, an Italian professional office tagged as telecom infrastructure with zero megawatts and no operator.

The entry carries no capacity figure, no operator, no website, and no suitability rating. Its name does the work instead. "Studio" in Italian usage denotes a professional or design practice, and "SRLS" is the simplified limited-liability form used by small startups, freelancers, and professional practices because of its lower minimum capital requirements. The same naming pattern appears in a Studio Delta Srl record elsewhere in the dataset, which points the same way.

For AI this is a measurement problem, not a power one. Any count of Italian data centers assembled from OpenStreetMap tags will absorb offices like this one, and each one inflates the apparent facility count without adding a megawatt of load. The building and grid constraints that bind AI scaling are simply not present at this scale, because a professional practice draws nothing comparable to a compute campus.

What the data does not say is how common this mistagging is, how many other points share the pattern, or anything about Italy's actual data-center capacity. It is one point, at zero megawatts, with no operator attached. It is evidence about tagging practice, not about compute.
